title_en: Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, Shi Shucheng v. Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News Agency — dispute over infringement of the right of reputation

full_text_en:
Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, Shi Shucheng v. Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News — dispute over infringement of reputation rights

Plaintiffs: Hu Jichao, male, 45 years old, cadre of the Propaganda Department of the CPC Chishui Municipal Committee, Guizhou Province.
Plaintiff: Zhou Kongzhao, male, 45 years old, cadre of the Chishui Cultural Center, Guizhou Province.
Plaintiff: Shi Shucheng, male, 57 years old, cadre of the Chishui Party School, Guizhou Province.

Defendant: Liu Shouzhong, male, 47 years old, cadre of Zunyi Television Station, Guizhou Province.
Defendant: Zunyi Evening News, Guizhou Province.
Legal representative: Che Peiying, Editor-in-Chief.

The plaintiffs Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, and Shi Shucheng filed a lawsuit with the Chishui People's Court of Guizhou Province against the defendants Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News regarding a dispute over infringement of reputation rights.

Plaintiffs' Allegations
The plaintiffs alleged that the three characters Hu Yizhao, Zhou Kongchao, and Shi Shuting in the book *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* created by defendant Liu Shouzhong were caricatures of the three plaintiffs; and that Zunyi Evening News published *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* in serial form, thereby damaging the reputation of the three plaintiffs. The plaintiffs requested the court to order defendants Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News to cease the infringement, make a public apology, eliminate the adverse effects, and compensate for losses.

Defendant's Defense
Defendant Liu Shouzhong argued that the characters Hu Yizhao, Zhou Kongchao, and Shi Shuting in *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* were purely fictional and, although sharing the same surnames with the three plaintiffs, had different given names, were born in different eras, had different social backgrounds, and held different identities. The defendant's work did not infringe upon the reputation rights of the three plaintiffs.

Defendant Zunyi Evening News argued that *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* belongs to the fiction genre, which allows the author to fabricate characters and plotlines, and the newspaper had no obligation to verify whether characters in the work were modeled on real persons or depicted actual individuals. The serialization of *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* by Zunyi Evening News did not infringe upon the plaintiffs' reputation rights.

Facts Found by the Court
The Chishui People's Court found through trial: Defendant Liu Shouzhong was originally a cadre of the Chishui Cultural Center in Guizhou Province and had previously worked in the same unit or system as the plaintiffs Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, and Shi Shucheng. Liu Shouzhong had previously had conflicts with the three plaintiffs over work-related issues. In 1988, when the Chishui Cultural Center was evaluating professional titles for its staff, a mimeographed anonymous leaflet appeared. The leaflet accused Liu Shouzhong of having problems and argued that he should not be granted a mid-level professional title. Liu Shouzhong suspected that the leaflet was written by the three plaintiffs and threatened to retaliate by publishing an article in print. From November of the same year, Zunyi Evening News began serializing Liu Shouzhong's long historical documentary novel *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng*. In early April 1989, Liu Shouzhong told some cadres in Chishui City to pay attention to the Zunyi Evening News in mid-April. On April 19 and 20, the serialized *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* in Zunyi Evening News featured three characters: drug dealer Hu Yizhao, brothel owner Zhou Kongchao, and local ruffian Shi Shuting. Not only did these three characters share the same surnames as the three plaintiffs, but the characters in their given names were either similar or homophonic. Many descriptive features of the three characters were identical or similar to those of the three plaintiffs. Defendant Liu Shouzhong portrayed these three characters extremely negatively. After *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* was published, readers familiar with the three plaintiffs immediately recognized that the author was insulting and caricaturing them. Defendant Liu Shouzhong once told others at the Chishui Cultural Center: "There are so many people, why did I single out these three to write about? There is a reason for that." On May 15 of the same year, the three plaintiffs jointly wrote a letter to the Editor-in-Chief of Zunyi Evening News, stating that the serialized *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* had infringed upon their reputation rights and requesting that Zunyi Evening News cease the serialization. However, Zunyi Evening News ignored the request and continued the serialization, causing the depictions of Hu Yizhao, Zhou Kongchao, and Shi Shuting in *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* to appear publicly on multiple occasions.

Opinion of the Court
The Chishui People's Court held: Literary and artistic creation is a freedom of citizens, and the state encourages and assists citizens in creative work beneficial to the people in the fields of literature and art. When exercising the right to freedom of literary and artistic creation, citizens shall not infringe upon the lawful freedoms and rights of other citizens. Article 101 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Citizens and legal persons enjoy the right of reputation. The personality dignity of citizens shall be protected by law, and it is prohibited to damage the reputation of citizens or legal persons by means such as insult or defamation." Defendant Liu Shouzhong, having long-standing conflicts with the three plaintiffs and suspecting that the anonymous mimeographed document attacking him originated from them, had threatened to retaliate by publishing a printed article. In creating *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng*, the defendant employed methods such as using identical surnames, similar given names, and prominent physical and appearance features to link the three characters in the work to the three plaintiffs and vilify them, making it immediately apparent to readers familiar with the three plaintiffs that these three negative characters were allusions to them. This caused adverse effects on the personal dignity of the three plaintiffs in the local area and damaged their reputation. After *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* was publicly published, the defendant also openly told others that there was a reason for writing the three plaintiffs into the novel. Therefore, the defendant's intent to infringe upon the reputation rights of the three plaintiffs was clear, and he should bear civil liability for the infringement in accordance with the law. The defendant's defense that the three characters in the work were purely fictional and did not infringe upon the plaintiffs' reputation rights could not be sustained. Defendant Zunyi Evening News, knowing that the serialized *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* had damaged the plaintiffs' reputation, continued the serialization, thereby expanding the harmful consequences, and should also bear certain civil liability.

Judgment
On March 19, 1991, the Chishui People's Court rendered the following judgment:
1. Defendant Liu Shouzhong shall make a public apology to plaintiffs Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, and Shi Shucheng in Zunyi Evening News;
2. The book *The Legend of Zhou Xicheng* shall not be published or distributed until the content infringing upon the reputation rights of plaintiffs Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, and Shi Shucheng has been deleted or revised;
3. Defendant Liu Shouzhong shall pay RMB 900 in compensation to plaintiffs Hu Jichao, Zhou Kongzhao, and Shi Shucheng; Zunyi Evening News shall pay RMB 300 in compensation to the plaintiffs.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, both Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News appealed to the Zunyi Intermediate People's Court, maintaining their original defense grounds.

The Zunyi Intermediate People's Court found through trial that the facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear and the applicable law was correct. The grounds of appeal of appellants Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News could not be sustained. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court dismissed the appeals of Liu Shouzhong and Zunyi Evening News and affirmed the original judgment.
